page_title: SparAMX: Accelerating Compressed LLMs Token Generation on AMX-powered CPUs

sources.entry: SparAMX: Accelerating Compressed LLMs Token Generation on AMX-powered CPUs - Measures decode kernels on a Xeon as DRAM-bound, so AMX pays at batch one only once bytes per token shrink, with code.

summary.title: SparAMX: Accelerating Compressed LLMs Token Generation on AMX-powered CPUs
summary.one_liner: Learn how combining Intel AMX matrix units with unstructured sparsity speeds up memory-bound LLM token decoding on CPUs, with open-source sparse kernels for PyTorch.
takeaways: LLM token decoding is memory-bound, which makes CPUs with AMX a viable target for acceleration.
Applying unstructured sparsity to linear layers with AMX gives a reported 1.42x end-to-end latency reduction versus the current PyTorch implementation.
The authors release open-source sparse kernels that automatically replace all linear layers in any PyTorch model.
Unstructured sparsity in the attention computation is shown for the first time, with a reported 1.14x speedup without accuracy loss.
summary.summary: This arXiv paper (submitted February 2025) argues that CPUs are a practical platform for LLM inference, especially in the memory-bound decoding stage. The authors use Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) on recent Xeon CPUs together with unstructured sparsity in model weights. They report a 1.42x end-to-end latency reduction over the current PyTorch implementation when applied to linear layers, and a 1.14x speedup from sparse attention computation without accuracy loss. The work ships open-source customized sparse kernels that can be swapped into any PyTorch model.
